$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of RFC 9162. Source .cache/rfc-9162.txt (RFC 9162, Certificate Transparency Version 2.0, sha256 a0e432ce7580c99fcc8faf0cf3f6191f9ce6b4864f949158e020d4ecb295081f). RFC 9162 Section 5 gives these messages in prose and ships no JSON Schema. INSTANCE: the JSON object POSTed to submit-entry (Section 5.1). submission, type and chain are all listed as Inputs and Section 4.2.1 says the submission, type, and chain inputs MUST be set as described in Section 5.1, so all three are required (inferred for chain: it may be an empty array). type is the integer 1 or 2 as Section 5.1 prints it; Section 4.5 gives x509_entry_v2 the value 0x0100 and precert_entry_v2 0x0101, which Section 5.1 calls the 'VersionedTransType integer value': the source disagrees with itself and this schema follows Section 5.1 and the badType error text (type is neither 1 nor 2). Instances are JSON values as received; binary fields stay base64 text and are not decoded (RFC 4648 Section 4, per Section 5). A pattern ^AQ[...] on a TransItem field binds the first two decoded octets, the VersionedTransType code of Section 4.5, because base64 of 0x01 0x0T begins AQ (every code here has 0 in its high nibble) and the low nibble T confines the third character to a block of four, its other two bits coming from the next octet; hence four characters per code in each pattern. The pattern states what a v2 log emits; it is not a client acceptance test, since a v2 client MUST NOT construe a non-v2 SCT (rfc-9162#R-0069) or an unrecognized TransItem type (rfc-9162#R-0079) as an error. Fields the RFC does not define are allowed (Section 5: any fields not understood SHOULD be ignored). A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. This schema cannot check the TransItem body, signatures, or any cross-field relation: those are in ../messages.yaml (constrained_by and notes per field).
